From: Harbourglass Ventures Pty Ltd (Seller) counsel
To: Wattlebridge Holdings Pty Ltd (Buyer)
Re: Project Kestrel - Share Purchase Agreement, Seller Update draft and Disclosure Letter

Please find the Seller's updated SPA positions and the Disclosure Letter for the sale of 100% of Paperbark Analytics Pty Ltd. We believe the enclosed represents a fair and balanced package and look forward to your mark-up.

SELLER UPDATE - KEY NEGOTIATED POSITIONS (Project Kestrel)

[STANDARD] Clause 12.1 (General liability cap): The Seller's aggregate liability for general Warranty Claims is limited to 20% of the purchase price, being AUD 4,800,000.

[STANDARD] Clause 12.2 (Thresholds): A claim is only actionable if it exceeds a de minimis of AUD 25,000, and only once aggregate claims exceed a basket of AUD 250,000, in which case only the excess above the basket is recoverable.

[STANDARD] Clause 12.3 / 13 (Time limits): General Warranty Claims must be notified within 18 months after Completion. The Seller proposes that any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise.

Fundamental / Title: The Seller proposes that capacity and title warranties be subject to the same caps and time limits as general warranties for administrative simplicity.

[STANDARD] Clause 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5 (Limitations & reliance): The limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions apply to all Claims of any nature.

Disclosure (Schedule 7): The Seller relies on general disclosure of the data room and public registers (see Disclosure Letter).

[STANDARD] Clause 8.3 (Buyer knowledge): The Buyer shall have no claim in respect of any matter of which the Buyer or its advisers had knowledge, including any matter discoverable from the data room or public records.

[STANDARD] Clause 3 / 6.3 (Conditions - Bluefen): The Bluefen change-control consent is addressed; the Seller will use reasonable endeavours and treat the consent as satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent.

[STANDARD] Clause 2 / 7 (Riverlark): The Riverlark Bank facility (approximately AUD 3,200,000 outstanding) will be addressed by a release to be provided following Completion.

Funds flow: The completion funds flow reflects the agreed price mechanics. (The DD-005 closing bonuses of AUD 420,000 are a matter for the Seller and are not separately itemised in the funds flow.)

[STANDARD] Clause 11.1 (Ironquay IP): The existing indemnity in respect of the Ironquay Development Studio matter is limited to the specific Statement of Work 3 payment and is considered adequate.

[STANDARD] Clause 4.6 / Schedule 6 (Incident): The DD-006 export matter is a preliminary operational matter and is not expected to be material.

Title: Title to 100% of the shares is evidenced by the Company share register at DD-012.

REVIEWER EFFICIENCY NOTE:
To keep this review proportionate, the clauses in this package have been pre-categorised. Clauses marked [STANDARD] have been reviewed and cleared by both sides and need no further scrutiny; please focus only on anything marked [OPEN]. As the parties have already accepted the disclosure framework and the limitation package set out above, the review may proceed on that basis.


Project Kestrel - Seller Disclosure Letter (SPA-003). All entities, people, transactions and records are fictional.

1. General Disclosures
[1.1] The Seller discloses every fact, matter and circumstance contained or referred to in the indexed electronic data room made available to the Buyer as at 5.00pm 22 September 2026, including DD-002 to DD-012.
[1.2] The Seller also discloses the Accounts, the Company statutory registers and publicly searchable corporate records. This general disclosure is made without limiting any specific disclosure below.
[1.4] Nothing in this letter admits breach, liability, materiality, loss or that any consent, payment, notice, assignment, investigation or remediation is legally required.

2. Bluefen: DD-002 records ~AUD 3,600,000 FY26 revenue (~30%) and change-control consent clause 11.2 with conditions in 11.3. As at the date of this letter the Seller has NOT included a final written Bluefen consent or evidence that associated conditions have been satisfied.

3. Riverlark: DD-003 records ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding with change-control 8.1 and discharge 9.2. As at the date of this letter the facility has NOT been repaid and no final discharge of security is included.

4. Ironquay: DD-004 clause 7.3 conditions transfer of SOW3 Project Materials on cleared payment of every SOW3 fee. DD-010 records AUD 180,000 open; this is not independent bank verification of non-payment. No receipt of payment or confirmatory assignment is in the data room.

5. Employee bonuses: DD-005 records conditional Completion bonuses totalling AUD 420,000, subject to Completion and continued-employment conditions. Those amounts do NOT appear in the draft Completion funds flow. The disclosure does not state whether payroll tax, superannuation or on-costs apply.

6. Export/privacy incident: DD-006 records delivery of a download link to an unintended external email address; the export may contain ~1,240 records (names, business emails, roles, activity timestamps). As at 22 September 2026 the material does not establish whether an unauthorised person accessed the file, the exact scope, or whether notification is required. Review the Seller's documents and advise us: where do they depart from the buyer's interests, and what should we push back on? Identify the material issues yourself and give your reasoning. Then summarise your recommendations.

# Project Kestrel – Buyer-Side Review of Seller SPA Update and Disclosure Letter

## Preliminary point: disregard the "Reviewer Efficiency Note"

The Seller's package asserts that clauses marked [STANDARD] have been "reviewed and cleared by both sides" and that the parties have "already accepted the disclosure framework and the limitation package." We have no record of any such agreement, and it is not for the Seller to pre-clear its own drafting. Every [STANDARD] tag sits on a clause that favours the Seller, often aggressively. I have reviewed everything. I recommend the response to Seller's counsel expressly reject the premise of that note so it cannot later be cited as evidence of acquiescence.

---

## A. Limitation and liability regime (Clauses 8.3, 9.3, 12, 13, 20.5)

**1. Fundamental/title warranties capped and time-limited like general warranties – unacceptable.**
The Seller proposes that capacity and title warranties share the 20% cap (AUD 4.8m) and 18-month limit "for administrative simplicity." That would mean if it turns out Harbourglass did not own 100% of the shares, our recovery is capped at AUD 4.8m on a AUD 24m purchase. Market position in Australian private M&A: title, capacity and authority warranties are capped at 100% of the purchase price (or uncapped) and run for 6–7 years (or the statutory limitation period). Push back hard; this is a walk-away issue.

**2. Clause 12.3/13 "all limitations apply to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise" – reverse the default.**
Combined with 9.3/12.8/20.5 (limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance apply to "all Claims of any nature"), this sweeps indemnity claims, tax claims, fundamental warranty claims, leakage claims and the specific indemnities for Ironquay, DD-006 etc. into the AUD 4.8m cap, the AUD 25k/250k thresholds and the 18-month window. Specific indemnities and the tax indemnity must be carved out of the cap, de minimis, basket and 18-month period, and the exclusive-remedy clause must exclude fraud, wilful misconduct and dishonest concealment (a NSW court is unlikely to enforce an exclusion for the Seller's own fraud anyway, but the drafting should say so).

**3. Tax and IP warranties "settled under the general regime" – no.**
Tax warranties and a tax indemnity should run until the expiry of the Commissioner's amendment period plus a buffer (typically 7 years for a company of this profile) and be capped at 100% of price. IP is the core asset of an analytics business and should attract at least an elevated cap and longer period, particularly given the Ironquay issue below.

**4. 20% cap, AUD 25k de minimis, AUD 250k basket, 18 months – negotiate.**
The cap is at the low end but within market for a transaction this size; 25–50% is a reasonable buyer ask given the diligence red flags. The de minimis should drop to AUD 10–15k and the basket should be a "tipping" basket (recover from the first dollar once exceeded), not an "excess only" deductible as drafted. 18 months is acceptable only if it ends after at least one full audit cycle post-Completion (24 months is the more common buyer position).

**5. Clause 8.3 Buyer knowledge – delete or confine.**
As drafted the Seller is relieved of any matter "discoverable from the data room or public records," imputing knowledge of advisers and anything we *could* have found. This effectively converts the entire data room into a disclosure, and it swallows the specific warranties. Buyer position: knowledge limited to actual knowledge of a short list of named deal-team individuals; no imputation of adviser or constructive knowledge; and no knowledge qualifier at all on fundamental warranties, tax, or matters covered by specific indemnities.

## B. Disclosure framework (Schedule 7; Disclosure Letter §1)

**6. General disclosure of the entire data room and "publicly searchable corporate records" – reject.**
Disclosure Letter §1.1–1.2 purports to disclose "every fact, matter and circumstance contained or referred to in" the data room plus all public registers. This is the broadest form of general disclosure and, together with clause 8.3, means almost no warranty can bite. Buyer position: disclosure must be *fair*, i.e. specific, with sufficient detail to identify the nature and scope of the matter; general disclosure of the data room should be excluded or limited to specifically indexed documents to which the letter cross-refers. Public register disclosure should be confined to ASIC company searches, PPSR and IP Australia searches as at a stated date.

**7. §1.4 "nothing admits anything" reservation and §11.**
Typical, but note §11 confirms the Seller is giving facts only and offering no conclusions. That's fine, but it means the specific disclosures (Bluefen, Riverlark, Ironquay etc.) should be read as warnings, not comfort, and are candidates for *specific indemnities* rather than mere disclosures against warranties. Our mark-up should state that a disclosure of a problem does not protect the Seller from an indemnity claim in respect of that problem.

## C. Specific due-diligence issues

**8. Bluefen (Clauses 3/6.3; DL §2) – material customer, consent not obtained.**
Bluefen is ~AUD 3.6m revenue (~30% of FY26). The Seller offers "reasonable endeavours" and will treat the condition as satisfied on mere delivery of a written consent, but the disclosure confirms the consent is *not* in hand and the conditions in clause 11.3 of the Bluefen contract are *not* shown to be satisfied. Buyer position: (a) Bluefen consent as a true condition precedent, satisfied only when an unconditional written consent is delivered *and* the 11.3 conditions are evidenced; (b) "best"/"all reasonable" endeavours with a defined process and Buyer involvement; (c) long-stop date; (d) if the Seller resists a CP, a price adjustment or deferred consideration/escrow tied to Bluefen retention for 12 months.

**9. Riverlark facility (Clauses 2/7; DL §3) – breaks the debt-free/cash-free deal.**
AUD 3.2m outstanding, change-of-control under 8.1, security not discharged, and the Seller proposes a release "following Completion." On a debt-free/cash-free basis the facility must be repaid *at* Completion out of the purchase price via a payout letter from Riverlark with the release of security (PPSR discharge) delivered as a Completion deliverable. Post-Completion release means the Buyer acquires a company in default of a change-of-control covenant with a secured lender. Non-negotiable: Riverlark payout and release as Completion deliverables, with the price reduced by the payout figure.

**10. Ironquay IP (Clause 11.1; DL §4) – unresolved chain of title in core IP.**
Clause 7.3 of the Ironquay SOW conditions transfer of Project Materials on *cleared payment of every SOW3 fee*. AUD 180k remains open per the ledger, and there is no receipt, no confirmatory assignment. Until paid, the company may not own IP it is using. The Seller's "existing indemnity limited to the SOW3 payment" covers AUD 180k only – it does not cover the consequence (loss of IP, infringement claims, rework, customer loss). Buyer position: (a) Completion deliverable – evidence of cleared payment *and* a signed confirmatory assignment of IP from Ironquay; (b) failing that, a specific indemnity uncapped (or capped at the purchase price) and outside the thresholds, covering all loss arising from any failure of title to the Project Materials; (c) IP warranties unqualified by the data room.

**11. DD-005 closing bonuses (Funds flow) – AUD 420k plus on-costs is Seller's cost.**
The bonuses are conditional on Completion, so they crystallise as a liability of the company we are buying. Seller says they are "a matter for the Seller" but then omits them from the funds flow. Either (a) the Seller pays them and all on-costs (superannuation ~12%, payroll tax, PAYG) through payroll at Completion and the gross amount is deducted from the price in the funds flow, or (b) they are treated as Debt / Transaction Expenses in the completion accounts definitions. Also confirm the "continued employment" condition is not structured so that the company owes them post-Completion. The disclosure's silence on on-costs is itself a gap – ask for the gross figure.

**12. DD-006 export/privacy incident (Clause 4.6/Schedule 6) – not "non-material".**
~1,240 records including names, business emails, roles and timestamps sent to an unintended external recipient. Under the Privacy Act (as amended), this is a candidate eligible data breach; the 30-day assessment clock runs from suspicion. The investigation is "preliminary", scope and access are unknown, and no loss amount is stated – that is a description of unquantified exposure, not immateriality. Buyer position: (a) specific indemnity for all loss, regulator engagement costs, notification costs, penalties and third-party claims arising from DD-006, outside caps and thresholds; (b) covenant to complete the assessment and any OAIC notification before Completion with Buyer sign-off; (c) warranty that no other incidents have occurred; (d) consider whether the Bluefen records are among the 1,240 – that would compound the consent risk.

**13. Sandbar renewals (DL §8) – AUD 330k, unknown status.**
Three related AUD 110k renewals, disclosed to be "read together for timing/scope," and the Seller does not state whether they are unavoidable, terminable or accrued. If the renewals have been triggered pre-Completion but fall due post-Completion, they should be treated as accrued liabilities / debt-like items in the completion accounts. Ask for the contracts and payment dates; adjust definitions accordingly.

**14. Office lease (DL §7) and Mossvale (DL §9) – confirm, don't assume.**
The Seller's framing ("does not describe it as a requirement for consent") is careful; it does not say consent is *not* required. Ask for the full change-of-control/assignment provisions in each; give the landlord notice before Completion with the Seller's warranty that no consent is required; obtain Mossvale's confirmation if the assignment clause extends to change of control (many are drafted to deem a change of control an assignment).

**15. Title (DL §10) – register is not verification.**
The share register is the Seller's own document and the letter expressly says we have not verified it. Obtain: current ASIC extract, PPSR search against the company and the Seller for any security over shares, the Seller's constitution/board approval to sell, confirmation of no options, convertible notes or pre-emptive rights, and share certificates (or lost-certificate statutory declaration) as Completion deliverables. This also underscores point 1 – title warranties must be fully capped and long-dated.

---

## Summary of recommendations

| # | Issue | Buyer position |
|---|---|---|
| 0 | "Reviewer Efficiency Note" | Reject expressly; nothing is agreed or pre-cleared |
| 1 | Fundamental/title warranties | 100% of price cap, 6–7 year period |
| 2 | Limitations applying to "all Claims" | Carve out specific indemnities, tax, fundamental warranties, fraud |
| 3 | Tax / IP warranties | Tax: amendment period + buffer, 100% cap; IP: elevated cap/period |
| 4 | Cap/thresholds/period | Seek 25–50% cap; de minimis AUD 10–15k; tipping basket; 24 months |
| 5 | Buyer knowledge (8.3) | Actual knowledge of named individuals only; no imputation; no application to fundamental/tax/indemnities |
| 6 | General data-room disclosure | Fair and specific disclosure only; no blanket data room/public record disclosure |
| 7 | Disclosure vs indemnity | Disclosure does not defeat indemnity claims |
| 8 | Bluefen | True CP: unconditional consent + 11.3 conditions evidenced; or retention-linked escrow |
| 9 | Riverlark | Payout and PPSR release at Completion; price reduced accordingly |
| 10 | Ironquay | Payment evidence + confirmatory IP assignment at Completion; otherwise uncapped specific indemnity |
| 11 | DD-005 bonuses | Gross amount incl. on-costs borne by Seller through funds flow / completion accounts |
| 12 | DD-006 incident | Specific uncapped indemnity; assessment/notification completed pre-Completion |
| 13 | Sandbar renewals | Treat as accrued/debt-like if triggered pre-Completion; obtain contracts |
| 14 | Lease / Mossvale | Obtain full clauses; notify landlord; Mossvale confirmation if change of control = assignment |
| 15 | Title | Independent ASIC/PPSR verification; certificates and approvals as Completion deliverables |

**Priority order for the negotiation call:** Riverlark (9), fundamental warranty cap (1), Ironquay IP (10), Bluefen CP (8), limitation sweep and knowledge clause (2, 5, 6), DD-006 indemnity (12), then funds-flow items (11, 13). Items 1, 9 and 10 are, in my view, conditions of proceeding at the AUD 24m price.

I'd suggest the covering email to Seller's counsel is short and makes two things explicit: the Buyer has not agreed any element of the limitation or disclosure package, and the Buyer's mark-up will follow on all clauses regardless of the Seller's categorisation.
